newsitem.title: USA: RTZ-CRA plans to boost US coal.
newsitem.headline: RTZ-CRA plans to boost US coal.

text.p: Anglo-Australian mining group RTZ-CRA plans to double its U.S. coal production capacity over the next 10 years, the president of RTZ-CRA's Kennecott Energy division, Gregory Boyce, said on Thursday.
The increase would take Kennecott's coal output, mostly based in the Powder Ridge Basin region of Wyoming and Montana, to about 85 million tonnes from the current 45 million, he said.
Boyce said low sulphur, or "compliance", coal producers such as Kennecott would benefit from a tightening of the U.S. Clean Air Act in the year 2000.

The new regulations would require that the levels of sulphur that can be emitted into the air by coal-fired power plants be reduced to 1.2 pounds per million British Thermal Units from the current 2.5 per million.
"Demand for compliance coals, we believe, is going to outstrip overall coals two-to-one," Boyce told reporters.
Boyce said U.S. electricity demand was growing at an average rate of about 2.5 percent a year, creating new opportunities for coal producers.

Faced with a general over-capacity in the Powder Ridge Basin, where about 260 million tonnes of coal is produced annually from a total of 16 mines, Kennecott has to squeeze as much out of a tonne of coal as it can, Boyce said.
Except for it 50 percent owned Decker mine in Montana, Kennecott employs non-union labor.
Boyce said this enabled the workforce to be more flexible in its ability to maximise output.
Degregulation of the U.S. power utilities industry is bringing to an end many of the lucrative long-term supply contracts enjoyed by the coal mining companies, Boyce said.
Long term contract prices of up to US$9 a tonne compare with spot prices running as low as US$4 a tonne, Boyce said.
Kennecott's Cordero and Antelope mines would account for a combined 60 million tonnes under the expansion with its Springs Creek mine producing 15 million tonnes.
The Colowyo deposit would be producing about six million tonnes a year and the Decker mine about five million, Boyce said.
